labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: correct. hiso_massAModel is literally the hiso of massA_singular_dec25_models (MassADEC25:396) and of existsUnique_causality_singularGX_dec25 at Xα := MassAModel, DY := massAModelCausality over the global family instance massAModelSingularGX. A probe under `import Causal` + `import CausalScaffold.EModelsBPrime` elaborated `(hiso_massAModel : ∀ o o' ψ, IsAEChart (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) ψ → ChartIso (massAModelCausality o) (massAModelCausality o') ψ)`, then existsUnique_causality_singularGX_dec25 (minkowski 2) massAModelCausality … hreg_massAModel hiso_massAModel hcov, and `massA_singular_all hcov = massA_singular_dec25_models hreg_massAModel hiso_massAModel hcov := rfl`. The case split is by (o, o'): (none, _) hiso_row_none, (some, none) hiso_column_none, (some, some) BPrimeEAlpha.hiso_family, whose IsAEChart under EAlphaGX.singularGXFamily is defeq to the family's (massAModelSingularGX_some is rfl). massA_singular_all, massA_causalite_models, existsUnique_isAtlasCausalityDEC25 carry only [SingularGXStructure (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) M] and hcov, which is DEC-25's E≥0-manifold. There is no hidden hypothesis: the section variables add none, and the local-instance sections change no hypothesis. The conclusions are l.1396 in DEC-25's sense, with « natural » = IsAtlasCausalityDEC25 and uniqueness among absolutely minimal causalities with an isomorphic chart at each point (OQ-18). existsUnique_isAtlasCausalityDEC25 also gives ∃! among natural causalities. The per-manifold theorems are universe-polymorphic (probed at Type (u+1)). forall_exists_massA_models is for N : Type only, inherited from forall_exists_massA_models_iff; it is the 'at once' form, and massA_causalite_models covers every universe. Sub-families: isAtlasCausalityDEC25_iff_e0 and _iff_ealpha are true iffs. Their right sides are exactly the properties that BPrimeE0.existsUnique_causality_e0 and BPrimeEAlpha.existsUnique_causality_ealpha give. Both proofs go through the uniqueness clause of massA_singular_all. Witnesses: massA_dec25_models_e0_sing (E₀ with E0GX.singularGX, Sing nonempty, identity X_A-chart, E0.causality natural over the whole family, cac, push-up, unique); massA_dec25_models_epi (E_π with EAlphaGX.singularGX π, defeq to the family's value, Sing = line nonempty, massive π natural over the whole family, uniqueness included); isAtlasCausalityDEC25_model and massA_singular_model at every model.

labels.label: defi:causal_Ealpha
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: correct. The row also carries the first sentence, the model sheaves, by earlier anchors, and κ = 0 is read as in OQ-34/OQ-35. causal_Ealpha_manifolds is l.1339–1340 at every E≥0-manifold: a natural causality (every chart of the maximal a.e. atlas and every X_A-chart a ChartIso), unique among absolutely minimal causalities with an isomorphic chart at each point (OQ-18), and I^±_U(x) open for every open U (U = ⊤ included), from the Causality fields isOpen_lt_right/left, which are the Lean form of the standing assumption at l.243. causal_Ealpha_e0_Iminus_eq_empty witnesses « possibly empty »: E0.causality is natural over the family, and I⁻_U(p) = ∅ for some p ∈ Sing(E₀) and every U. causal_Ealpha_lt_singLine transports the ordering half of singLine_locallyChronal through an X_A-chart into E_κ, κ > 0. The conclusion is not vacuous: C.lt W a b forces a, b ∈ W, and ε > 0. Quantified over every x on the line and every W ∋ x, it also gives the CurveOn (chronal-curve) form of s ↦ e.symm (s, apex) locally, so « locally chronal » is fairly confirmed. eq_massAModelCausality_of_chartIso: the strong claim checked. Its only hypothesis is that every X_A-chart out of the model is a ChartIso. There is no minimality, and no condition on the maximal-atlas charts, so the uniqueness class is wider than the paper's « inducing that of E_α in every chart » at M = the model. The proof uses only the identity chart (isAEChart_refl) and eq_of_chartIso_refl (GXStructure:643), which is sound because ChartIso at refl constrains every open set. The claim is correct, but only at the models themselves; the REPORT's « (a manifold covered by one chart) » overstates this (see findings). hiso_massAModel and chartIso_models_some_some are as for cor:massA_causalite.

findings_review.finding: Finding 1 (cor:massA_causalite #1): the proof (l.1399–1406) checks neither hreg ((b) second half, l.620) nor (b′) (step (B), l.631–632, OQ-64). Both hold at the E≥0 models, so this is a missing citation; prop:isom (BTZ_1.tex:378–383) and its first step (l.446) could be cited.
findings_review.notes: Line numbers checked. ETT l.1396–1406 is the corollary and its proof; l.620 is (b); l.631–632 is the « isomorphisms of the model spaces » of step (B); BTZ_1.tex:378–383 is prop:isom (α, β ∈ ℝ₊, α ≠ 2π, U open connected containing a singular point, φ an a.e. E-morphism and local homeomorphism ⇒ α = β, φ a rotation-translation, l.373); BTZ_1.tex:446 is the first step of its proof (elliptic vs parabolic holonomy ⇒ β > 0 iff α > 0). Both model facts are proved in Lean (hreg_massAModel, hiso_massAModel). One caveat in the cited source, already recorded in defi:causal_Ealpha's row (« At α = 2πn, n ≥ 2, the linear holonomy is trivial »): at α ∈ 2πℤ, α ≥ 4π, l.446's « elliptic » should read « elliptic or trivial ». The conclusion β > 0 survives, since a trivial holonomy is not parabolic. E₀ → E₀ via prop:isom rests on its « mutatis mutandis » (l.447), whose l.459 step does not carry over verbatim (already a cor:massA_causalite paper_finding). Lean proves the cross-type case by causality, not holonomy (MassAModelsInstance.notMem_axis_of_isAEChart).

Finding 3 (defi:causal_Ealpha #1): the definition asserts a theorem at l.1339–1340, 57 lines before cor:massA_causalite (l.1396), with no reference to prop:GX_sing_espace_temps_topo, and it rests on hreg and (b′), which it does not mention.
findings_review.kind: paper, statement-level; citation (a claim inside a definition, missing forward reference)
findings_review.notes: 1396 − 1339 = 57 is right, measured to the corollary's statement. The proof starts at l.1399, 60 lines on. Two wording fixes. (1) « stated 57 lines earlier » reads as if the corollary came first; it is the definition that comes 57 lines before the corollary. (2) cor:massA_causalite states existence only. The definition's « unique » is prop:GX_sing_espace_temps_topo's (l.622), reached through « natural », and its openness clause is the standing assumption of l.243. So the sentence is cor:massA_causalite together with the uniqueness of prop:GX_sing_espace_temps_topo, not the corollary alone. This is not an error: the claim is true in the readings and is proved here.

findings_review.finding: defi:causal_Ealpha #2: at a model, « unique » holds outright, absolutely minimal or not, because the identity is an X_A-chart. OQ-18's counterexample is on ℝ ⊔ ℝ, not on an E≥0-manifold.
findings_review.notes: eq_massAModelCausality_of_chartIso checked; see the labels entry. OQ-18's row does say « fails on ℝ ⊔ ℝ ». The REPORT's parenthesis « At a model (a manifold covered by one chart) » overstates: the theorem is for M = MassAModel o only. A manifold covered by one X_A-chart, such as an open subset of a model, is not stated, although the same eq_of_agreeOn argument applies.

findings_review.finding: Finding 4 (defi:causal_Ealpha #3): « I^±(x) is always an open subset » needs no argument, because openness of ≪ is a standing assumption (defi:causalite, l.243). « Possibly empty » happens at BTZ points.
findings_review.notes: l.243 reads « Openness of ≪ is a standing assumption of this work », inside defi:causalite (l.237–252). In Lean this is the Causality fields isOpen_lt_right/isOpen_lt_left (Causality.lean:77–84), so a causality, once its existence is proved, is open. Here that existence is massA_singular_all. « Possibly empty » is causal_Ealpha_e0_Iminus_eq_empty (E0.Iminus_axis), in line with defi:causal_E0, l.1347.

findings_review.finding: defi:causal_Ealpha #4: « For α > 0 the singular line is timelike, hence locally chronal » (l.1341), confirmed at every E≥0-manifold through X_A-charts into E_κ, κ > 0.
findings_review.notes: causal_Ealpha_lt_singLine. « Timelike » itself is anchored at the models (singLine_chronalCurveOn, already in the row).

findings_review.finding: Finding 6 (cor:massA_causalite #2): natural over E≥0 ⇔ natural over {E₀} (resp. over {E_κ}_{κ>0}). « So the causality generated by an X_A-atlas does not depend on whether A is read as the models the manifold uses or as all of [0, ∞). »
findings_review.kind: confirmation (bears on def:singular_spacetime, l.1501–1504); overstated as written
findings_review.notes: The two iffs are proved (isAtlasCausalityDEC25_iff_e0, _iff_ealpha) for A = {0} and A = (0, ∞). The general sentence, for an arbitrary A ⊂ ℝ₊ such as {0, π}, is true by the same ten-line argument: the family's natural causality exists by massA_singular_all, a causality natural over A is absolutely minimal with an isomorphic chart at each point, so the uniqueness clause applies. But it is not stated in Lean. Before it goes to the author, restrict it to the two sub-families, or say « by the same argument, formalized for A = {0} and A = (0, ∞) ». Cite def:singular_spacetime (l.1501–1504, where A ⊂ ℝ₊ enters) rather than l.1396.

question.details: OQ-18 (registers/DECISIONS.md:175, OPEN) asks whether the sheaf clause of defi:causalite is meant as gluing (so absolute minimality), or whether « unique » should read « unique absolutely minimal ». That is the question for every « unique causality » claim in the paper. « A unique causal structure inducing that of E_α in every chart » (l.1339) is prop:GX_sing_espace_temps_topo's uniqueness (l.622) at the E≥0 models, and OQ-18 already blocks that label. A ruling on OQ-18 settles l.1339 and cor:massA_causalite's « natural » with no further question. No DEC applies, OQ-18 being open. OQ-87 is not needed. « Extending OQ-18 » is not an available action: the register header says rows are never edited once committed, and tools/registers.py check fails if one is. It is not needed either, because both rows' blocked_on already name OQ-18 (defi:causal_Ealpha « the readings of … « unique » », cor:massA_causalite « OQ-18 (« natural ») »). Keep OQ-18 in the new blocked_on texts below with the line numbers (l.1339, l.1396).

findings.what: « So the causality generated by an X_A-atlas does not depend on whether A is read as the models the manifold uses or as all of [0, oo) » is stated as a consequence of the two Lean iffs. Those iffs cover A = {0} and A = (0, ∞) only, so a general A ⊂ ℝ₊ is not formalized. The claim is true by the same argument, so this is not a false finding.
findings.fix: At curation write: « ETT.tex:1396 « natural », and def:singular_spacetime (l.1501–1504): at an E₀-manifold, resp. an E_{>0}-manifold, a causality is natural over E_{≥0} iff it is natural over {E₀} (isAtlasCausalityDEC25_iff_e0), resp. over {E_κ}_{κ>0} (isAtlasCausalityDEC25_iff_ealpha). So for A = {0} and A = (0, ∞) the causality generated by the X_A-atlas is the same as for A = [0, ∞); for a general A ⊂ ℝ₊ the same argument applies (the uniqueness clause of massA_singular_all), not formalized. »
